Make one object the controller owner of another

Source: R/operator_helpers.R
set_owner.Rd

Adds an ownerReferences entry to obj pointing at owner, with controller: true. Kubernetes then deletes obj when owner is deleted, and a Manager controller that owns obj's kind reconciles owner whenever obj changes. Use it on objects before you kube_apply() them.

Usage

set_owner(obj, owner, controller = TRUE, block_owner_deletion = TRUE)

Arguments

obj

The object to own (a manifest list).

owner

The owning object, as returned by kube_get(); it needs metadata$uid.

controller

Mark the owner as the controller (only one owner can be).

block_owner_deletion

With foreground deletion, keep the owner until this object is gone.

Value

obj with the owner reference added (an existing reference to the same owner is replaced).

Details

Owner references cannot cross namespaces, so if obj has no namespace it gets the owner's.

Examples

owner <- list(apiVersion = "example.com/v1", kind = "Site",
              metadata = list(name = "blog", namespace = "web", uid = "1234"))
cm <- list(apiVersion = "v1", kind = "ConfigMap",
           metadata = list(name = "blog-config"))
set_owner(cm, owner)$metadata$ownerReferences
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$apiVersion
#> [1] "example.com/v1"
#> 
#> [[1]]$kind
#> [1] "Site"
#> 
#> [[1]]$name
#> [1] "blog"
#> 
#> [[1]]$uid
#> [1] "1234"
#> 
#> [[1]]$controller
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> [[1]]$blockOwnerDeletion
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#>
